idiom_name: private-flag constructor guard + frozen validated instance (module-scope WeakSet brand)
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no private constructors, so the two enforcement halves of the Essence are simulated with its own integrity machinery: a module-scope WeakSet brand proves that an instance was built by the guarded constructor, and a static #constructing flag makes direct `new` throw while only the Essence's create() passes the flag and may instantiate. The classic two-class split collapses: Essence and CreationTarget live in one ES module that exports only the Essence, so the module boundary replaces friend/package-private coupling; Object.freeze() in the guarded constructor guarantees the compulsory properties stay immutable after creation. The classic explicit form is still justified when targets must be reusable across modules with multiple Essence permutations or when subclassing must be supported, since private elements are not inherited and the flag guard does not extend for free.
pitfalls: The static #constructing guard is process-global per class: reentrant or concurrent asynchronous creation interleaving between flag set and reset can let a second, unvalidated `new` slip through; the module-scope WeakSet brand check is reentrancy-safe and should back every public method.

Object.freeze is shallow: nested objects handed to the constructor stay mutable, so deep invariants need a deepFreeze walk; and writes to a frozen object fail silently in sloppy mode, throwing TypeError only in strict code (ES modules and class bodies are always strict, embedded sloppy scripts are not).

A forged instance via Reflect.construct(Contract, [], Contract) or a Proxy passes instanceof but carries no brand; only the WeakSet has() check (or an in-target private-field probe) detects it, so brand checks must not be skipped in methods.

Private elements are not inherited and cannot be accessed in subclass bodies, so extending a guarded CreationTarget forces an explicit super()-protocol redesign rather than a natural extension; validateParameters()-style feedback should throw TypeError/RangeError rather than return booleans, which invite truthiness checks.
